3. KEY-ENCODING ATTACK (logs/wb_test.txt, tools/verify_keys.rs — appended to a separate copy tree_wb, never to the deliverable)
White-box test against the PRODUCTION glue encode_k/exact_k with both kernels (Avx2 and Scalar), not just the cfg(test) Domain::exact: for 11 domains (bare, prefixes 'u','0','a','f','z','U','"',' ',0xff,'\r'), 10,543–17,573 samples each (crafted: lengths 1..40 of '0'/'z'/'f'/'9', base-36 and hex runs, leading zeros, all 32-hex corner values incl. hi=0, hi=2^64-1, fffffffffffffffe..., 31/33/16/30-char hex, upper-case at various positions, 'g' lookalikes, short prefixes of long IDs, prefix-doubled, other-prefix, spaces, \r, \t, control bytes, UTF-8, 300-char, plus 1,400 random strings with truncations/mutations; each sample also with the domain prefix prepended once and twice and with 'x'/'u' prepended). Checks, all passed: Avx2 == Scalar; result independent of junk bytes after the field (0,'0','f','z',',','\n',0xff); lookup == encode; class invariants (short: 1..11 [0-9a-z], len recovered; long: exactly 32 [0-9a-f], hi∉{0,MAX}; odd otherwise); never Key::default(); bytes_of roundtrip exact; ALL PAIRS (up to 309M per domain): domain.cmp(k_a,k_b) == a.cmp(b) and k_a==k_b iff a==b; sort by cmp yields strict byte order; no 64-bit hash collisions. Second test: People::build naming across classes (short/long/odd/upper/space/\r members, each as pivot) always picks the byte-wise smallest. 2 passed, 281 s.
Static review of id.rs/scan.rs kernels confirms the math: short rank = left-aligned base-36 over 11 positions ×36 + length (lo order == byte order incl. prefix/length ties); AVX2 maddubs/madd constants (36,1296) and 16-nibble packing with byte swap match the scalar functions; short-vs-long compare via long_rank12 proven correct for every first-difference position.

6. OBSERVATIONS (not defects, not blocking)
a) Equal-ingest copies with DIFFERENT content (which the rules exclude: "Copies with equal ingest_ts are identical") are resolved first-seen, so the kept copy depends on thread/chunk order. Found by an early version of my big crafted set that violated the contract (logs/repro_big.txt): NCPU=3/6 sometimes differed from ref.py on event e6b7f153a9e32e7b893fe52f28aa92810 (two copies, same ingest, different user/type). rel17 shows the identical flip on the same data (3 of 4 multi-thread runs), so semantics are unchanged from rel17 and the outcome is undefined by the rules. Deterministic at NCPU=1. The corrected suite (contract-conforming) is what section 4 reports.
b) The rerun cleanup removes every regular file or symlink named *.parquet in both output folders (including names starting with '_', which the rules say are ignored anyway); non-parquet files, dotfiles and subdirectories are left alone. Harmless.
c) In the engineer's own A/B log (v5c/logs/ab_rel17_c5.txt) rel17 round 0 shows exit 256; in my 5 rounds every rel17 and v1 run exited 0, so it was a transient on their side, not a binary problem.
